strings.d1.s0.name: Tiananmen Square
strings.d1.s0.tips: The world's largest public square. Expect a passport check and a security queue; visit the Mao Mausoleum in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Forbidden City
strings.d1.s1.tips: The Ming-Qing palace. Book online 7 days ahead with your passport (WeChat or the official site; tickets sell out). Walking south to north takes 3.5 hours. Closed on Mondays.
strings.d1.s2.name: Jingshan Park
strings.d1.s2.tips: A hill north of the Forbidden City with 360° views over the golden roofs.
strings.d1.s3.name: Siji Minfu Peking Duck
strings.d1.s3.tips: Peking duck next to Jingshan, better and cheaper than Quanjude. Expect a queue.
strings.d1.s4.name: Beihai Park
strings.d1.s4.tips: The imperial lake and the White Dagoba; rent a rowing boat.
strings.d1.b0.name: Quanjude Qianmen
strings.d1.b0.tips: The Peking duck institution since 1864; touristy but historic.
strings.d1.b1.name: National Museum of China
strings.d1.b1.tips: A huge museum on Tiananmen Square; free entry, a good option if you have no Forbidden City ticket.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mutianyu Great Wall
strings.d2.s0.tips: In summer, set off early at 08:30 (32°C). Take the cable car and toboggan, and bring water.
strings.d2.s1.name: Mutianyu Village Restaurant
strings.d2.s1.tips: A village restaurant below the wall serving trout and dumplings.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hongluo Temple
strings.d2.s2.tips: A mountain temple in Huairou, on the way back.
strings.d2.b0.name: Jinshanling Great Wall
strings.d2.b0.tips: A wilder, emptier stretch of wall, 2.5 hours away; best for hikers.
strings.d2.b1.name: Subway Restaurant Mutianyu
strings.d2.b1.tips: Fast food at the tour entrance; an alternative to the village restaurant.
strings.d3.theme: Temple of Heaven and the hutongs
strings.d3.s0.name: Temple of Heaven
strings.d3.s0.tips: The blue-roofed Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests. In the morning, retirees fill the park with tai chi, dancing and racket games.
strings.d3.s1.name: Qianmen Street
strings.d3.s1.tips: A restored Qing-style street, with the Dashilan side alleys nearby.
strings.d3.s2.name: Liqun Roast Duck
strings.d3.s2.tips: A legendary duck restaurant in a hutong. Book ahead; it is run-down but good.
strings.d3.s3.name: Shichahai & Houhai Lake
strings.d3.s3.tips: Walk around the lake: boats in summer, ice skating in winter.
strings.d3.s4.name: Nanluoguxiang Hutong
strings.d3.s4.tips: A touristy hutong street; the side alleys hide real courtyard homes. A rickshaw tour costs 100 CNY.
strings.d3.b0.name: Mr. Shi's Dumplings Nanluoguxiang
strings.d3.b0.tips: Dumplings, as an alternative to duck.
strings.d3.b1.name: Drum and Bell Towers
strings.d3.b1.tips: A performance at the Drum Tower; an alternative to the lake.
strings.d4.s0.name: Summer Palace
strings.d4.s0.tips: Kunming Lake and the Long Corridor. It is quiet in the morning. A boat costs 20 CNY; don't miss the Marble Boat.
strings.d4.s1.name: Summer Palace Suzhou Street
strings.d4.s1.tips: A canal street inside the palace grounds; good for snacks.
strings.d4.s2.name: 798 Art District
strings.d4.s2.tips: Galleries in old factories: UCCA (60 CNY), graffiti and cafés.
strings.d4.s3.name: 798 Café Timezone 8
strings.d4.s3.tips: A café in the art district.
strings.d4.b0.name: Old Summer Palace Yuanmingyuan
strings.d4.b0.tips: The ruins of the burned palace; an alternative to 798.
strings.d4.b1.name: Nuage Vietnamese Houhai
strings.d4.b1.tips: Vietnamese food by the lake; an evening option.
strings.d5.s0.name: Lama Temple Yonghegong
strings.d5.s0.tips: A Tibetan Buddhist temple with an 18 m Maitreya carved from a single tree. Incense is included in the ticket.
strings.d5.s1.name: Confucius Temple Beijing
strings.d5.s1.tips: Quiet courtyards and stelae, plus Guozijian Street.
strings.d5.s2.name: Wudaoying Hutong
strings.d5.s2.tips: A hip hutong with cafés and vegan food, next to the Lama Temple.
strings.d5.s3.name: Wangfujing
strings.d5.s3.tips: A shopping street with Oriental Plaza and a bookshop.
strings.d5.s4.name: Ghost Street Gui Jie
strings.d5.s4.tips: A 24-hour food street lit by red lanterns; try malaxiaolongxia (spicy crayfish) and hot pot.
strings.d5.b0.name: Haidilao Hot Pot Wangfujing
strings.d5.b0.tips: A hot pot chain famous for its service.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ditan Park
strings.d5.b1.tips: The park around the Temple of Earth; an alternative to the Confucius Temple.
strings.d6.theme: Ming Tombs and the Olympic Park
strings.d6.s0.name: Ming Tombs Changling
strings.d6.s0.tips: One hour from the city; the tombs of 13 emperors and the Sacred Way statues.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sacred Way Ming Tombs
strings.d6.s1.tips: A road lined with stone animals and statues of officials.
strings.d6.s2.name: Changping Village Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: Village food on the way back; try the jiaozi (dumplings).
strings.d6.s3.name: Olympic Park Bird's Nest
strings.d6.s3.tips: The 2008 Bird's Nest and Water Cube. Free from outside; 50 CNY to go inside.
strings.d6.s4.name: Olympic Forest Park
strings.d6.s4.tips: A huge park for walking, with a lake.
strings.d6.b0.name: Water Cube Restaurant
strings.d6.b0.tips: Right next to the Water Cube.
strings.d6.b1.name: Juyongguan Great Wall
strings.d6.b1.tips: A wall pass near the Ming Tombs; a second Great Wall day.
strings.d7.s0.name: Ritan Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: A park in the old embassy district; tai chi in the morning.
strings.d7.s1.name: Sanlitun Taikoo Li
strings.d7.s1.tips: Modern shopping, an Apple store and cafés.
strings.d7.s2.name: Jing-A Brewing Sanlitun
strings.d7.s2.tips: Beijing craft beer and burgers; a farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: Beijing Capital Airport Express Dongzhimen
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport express takes 25 minutes; for Daxing, go from Caoqiao.
strings.d7.b0.name: Xian Lao Man Dumplings
strings.d7.b0.tips: A dumpling chain; a cheap farewell meal.
strings.d7.b1.name: Silk Street Market
strings.d7.b1.tips: A market for knock-offs and silk. Haggle; an alternative to Taikoo Li.
strings.note0: The metro costs 3-9 CNY and is extensive, with English signage. Use Didi taxis (via Alipay). The airport express leaves from Dongzhimen. For Mutianyu and the Ming Tombs, take a tour or a Didi.
strings.note1: Visa: in 2026 many countries get 30 days visa-free (check for Türkiye). Alipay and WeChat Pay work with foreign cards. Set up a VPN beforehand.
strings.note2: Summer is 32-35°C and humid, with rain in July and August. Visit the Wall and palaces at 08:00, and use museums and malls at midday. Air pollution is low in summer.
strings.note3: The Forbidden City and Mao Mausoleum require your passport. Forbidden City tickets sell out online 7 days ahead. Closed on Mondays.
strings.note4: Peking duck costs 200-300 CNY (for 2), jiaozi 30-60 CNY, hot pot 150 CNY. Tipping is not expected. A street jianbing (savoury crepe) breakfast costs 10 CNY.
strings.note5: Google and WhatsApp don't work; Baidu Maps or Apple Maps do.
